question: In ΔABC, AB = 7 cm, BC = 10 cm, and AC = 8 cm. If AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, where D is a point on BC, then (DC)/(4) (in cm) is equal to:
solution:
**Given data:**

AB= 7 cm, AC= 8 cm, BC= 10 cm

AD bisects ∠BAC i.e., ∠BAD = ∠DAC

**Concept used:**

We would use the angular bisector theorem to proceed with the problem. According to the angular bisector theorem, the angle bisector of a triangle divides the opposite side of the angle in a proportion equal to the remaining sides of the triangle. In the Δ PQR, PS is the angular bisector of ∠QPR.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a953c03e0395fc14cb703f0de1dd3f118bedf8866209639c5375f49faa7d1ec.png] 

⇒ QSover SR = PQover PR (By angular bisector theorem)

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9baea2c47f632c6705b20c1f222bf7bf8f22db60b188f0cfd50f88ad4f57b9cf.png] 

In ΔABC, if AD bisects ∠BAC, then

⇒ ABover AC = BDover DC

Substituting the values of AB, AC, and BD as 10-DC

⇒ 7over8 = 10-DCover DC

Solving, we get-

⇒ 7 DC = 80 - 8 DC

⇒ 15 DC = 80

⇒ DC = 80over 15 or 16over 3

⇒ DCover 4 = 16over 3*4 = 4over 3

**Hence, DCover 4 equals 4over 3 cm.**
